NONE: › used to emphasize an adjective
（用於強調形容詞）

example: Julie's brother's so handsome it's not true.
朱莉的哥哥帥得令人難以置信。

NONE: › used to say that it is necessary to accept the situation as it exists
（用於表示有必要接受目前的處境）就接受吧

example: If she wants to spend all her money on clothes, so be it!
如果她想把錢都花在衣服，就由她去吧。

NONE: › used to make a promise in a very formal and serious way
上帝作證，我發誓

example: Everything I have said is true, so help me God.
上帝作證，我說的一切都是真的。

NONE: › goodbye
再會，再見
C2 used to express disappointment at the fact that a situation is not as you thought it was
（表示失望或惱火）…到此為止，…只好作罷

example: The car won't start. So much for our trip to the beach.
汽車又出毛病了，我們去海邊的旅程只好作罷。

NONE: › an amount that you do not know or state exactly
那麼多

example: By the time you've paid so much for the ferry and so much for the train fare, it would be cheaper to go by plane.
到頭來你為船費和火車費付了那麼多錢，還不如坐飛機便宜呢。

NONE: › to such a great degree
到…程度

example: It was a great project, so much so that it won first prize.
這一項目非常出色，以至於得了頭獎。

NONE: › used to say that a particular action or situation would be even more successful
那樣會更好

example: If you can go there this afternoon, so much the better.
如果你今天下午去那裡會更好。

NONE: › used for emphasis, or to show that something is being done against someone else's wishes
（表示強調或與某人的願望相反）事情就是這樣，沒甚麽可說的

example: Mine's bigger than yours, so there!
我的比你大，本來就是這樣！
No, I won't help you, so there!
不，我不會幫你的，沒甚麽好說的了！

NONE: C2 used to explain that what you are saying is not to be understood exactly as stated
姑妄言之，可以說

example: In that relationship it's very much Lorna who wears the trousers, so to speak (= Lorna makes all the important decisions).
可以這麽說，他們家裡基本上是洛娜說了算。

NONE: › used to mean "it's not important" and "I don't care"
那又怎樣？

example: So what if I'm 35 and I'm not married - I lead a perfectly fulfilling life!
我35歲還沒結婚，那又怎樣？——我的生活十分充實！
"Andrew won't like it, you know." "So what? - I don't care what Andrew thinks!"
「你知道，安德魯不會喜歡的。」「那又怎樣？——我不在乎安德魯是怎麽想的！」

U: › [ U ] used instead of a particular name to refer to someone or something, especially when the real name is not important or you have forgotten it

C: › [ C ] a polite way of referring to an unpleasant person
令人討厭的人，令人不快的人

example: She always keeps me up to date with the latest gossip - you know, so-and-so from down the road is having a baby and so-and-so's just bought a car.
她總會把最新的小道消息及時告訴我——你知道嗎，馬路那邊的某某人懷了孕，某某人剛買了汽車。
Mr Baker was such a so-and-so - he was always really mean!
貝克先生真是個討厭的傢夥——他總是十分刻薄！

NONE: B2 used to show that you think a word that is used to describe someone or something is not suitable or not correct
所謂的，號稱的
B2 used to introduce a new word or phrase that is not yet known by many people
叫做…的，名叫…的；所謂的

example: It was one of his so-called friends who supplied him with the drugs that killed him.
是他一個所謂的朋友提供毒品給他，讓他因此喪命。
It isn't yet clear how dangerous these so-called "super-rats" are.
目前還不清楚這種名叫「超級老鼠」的東西有多危險。

NONE: › between average quality and low quality; not good or well
一般（的），不好不壞（的）

example: a so-so performance
一般的表現
